daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

Former education minister Nadiem Makarim was sentenced to 10 years in prison in a major corruption case involving the procurement of Chromebooks for schools. The court found that the project caused state losses of Rp 1.56 trillion, and Makarim was also ordered to pay compensation of Rp 809.5 billion. In emotional scenes outside the courtroom, Makarim held back tears, saying he did not know who else to turn to for help, while his lawyers shouted protests as the judges left the courtroom immediately after reading the verdict.

  • The KPK conducted a major operation in Kuantan Singingi regency, Riau, arresting 10 people including the wife of Bupati Suhardiman Amby in a bribery case related to the appointment of a regional secretary, with the bupati and the sitting sekda initially evading authorities before eventually surrendering to the KPK.
  • The KPK questioned former Youth and Sports Minister Dito Ariotedjo regarding the background of additional hajj quotas from Saudi Arabia.
  • The KPK grilled Pemuda Pancasila chairman Japto Soerjosoemarno about his receipt of various assets in the Rita Widyasari corruption case, with the anti-graft body disclosing seized assets related to coal gratification.
  • President Prabowo will serve as inspecting officer at the peak commemoration of the 80th Bhayangkara Day in Cikeas, with the National Police explaining why the event will be held in Cikeas rather than at Monas.
  • The Public Works Minister praised the president's decision to establish a dedicated Hajj Ministry following the 2026 pilgrimage season.
  • PDI-P highlighted a controversial incident in which former president Jokowi stepped on a buffalo head during a PSI event, prompting clarification from the party.
  • The Constitutional Court rejected a challenge by civil servants against the requirement to serve at least 10 years before being eligible for transfer.

Foreign Policy & Defence

The Indonesian Embassy in Paris welcomed an Indonesian Garden in France as a means to strengthen cultural diplomacy. The development marks a new chapter in Indonesia-France cultural ties and public diplomacy efforts in Europe.

  • Indonesia is targeting the Singapore market for exports of surplus eggs and chicken meat.
  • Indonesia views its partnership with Russia as key to economic transformation.
  • New Zealand is ready to help Indonesia strengthen national dairy production.
  • The government is working to repatriate an Indonesian migrant worker from Cianjur who went viral after calling for help from Libya.

Other

The government announced that electricity tariffs will not increase for the July-August-September quarter. Separately, fuel prices saw adjustments as Pertamax Turbo and aviation fuel prices decreased starting 1 July, with BP Ultimate Diesel falling sharply and Pertamina Dex also declining, while Shell diesel dropped drastically to Rp 21,340 per liter.

  • The government explained that the tax on JHT withdrawals cannot yet be abolished, amid waves of criticism from labor groups rejecting the JHT tax.
  • Jakarta Governor Pramono announced the capital opened 2,843 job vacancies and received 100,000 applications in a single day, while the city plans to issue bonds worth Rp 3.5 trillion.
  • Indonesia expects GovTech to save over $84 billion in state spending.
  • Meta deactivated 185,000 Indonesian underage accounts as part of its child safety enforcement.
  • Police seized 18 tons of illegal cyanide destined for unlicensed mines.
  • The Attorney General's Office stated that restitution for sexual violence victims has not been sufficient to restore trauma, and strictly prohibited sexual violence cases from being resolved through restorative justice.
